Summary (high level):
- Live data deletion: immediate logical deletion/tombstone on the serving layer.
- Standard backup/snapshot retention: snapshots are immutable; they are retained for configured snapshot windows (typically 30/90/365 days depending on the account tier).
- Deletion propagation: tombstoned objects remain in existing snapshots until those snapshots age out, then a sweep process removes references; full physical erasure across all replicated backups typically completes within 30-90 days for Hosted (shorter if the account is on Dedicated and we perform an accelerated purge).
- KMS key revocation: revoking KMS keys renders encrypted snapshots unrecoverable, but for attestation/legal purposes we provide a key-revocation timeline and deletion attestation rather than relying purely on crypto-sanitization.

Thanks for the ping — happy to flush out the operational details. I'll break this into components.

1) Serving layer (live data)
- When a delete request is processed via the API, the object is marked deleted (tombstone) immediately in the metadata store. Reads will no longer return the object and downstream processes treat it as deleted.

2) Snapshots and backups
- Incremental snapshots: we take incremental snapshots every 6–12 hours for high-availability clusters; full snapshots are scheduled weekly. Snapshots are immutable once written.
- Retention windows: default hosted tiers retain snapshots for 90 days; some accounts have 30 or 365 day settings. Dedicated customers can request custom windows.
- Replication: snapshots are copied asynchronously across configured DR regions; replication lag is typically minutes to an hour depending on snapshot size.

3) Deletion propagation and purge mechanics
- Because snapshots are immutable, deleted data will remain in any snapshot taken prior to deletion until that snapshot is expired by retention policy.
- We run a background GC/sweep that removes references to deleted objects from active stores once all snapshots that reference them have expired; this sweep runs continuously but physical erasure of blocks (zeroing/reclaiming storage) is batched and depends on storage backend (may take an additional 48–72 hours after final reference removal).
- Typical timelines (Hosted US region, no legal hold):
   • Best case: if deletion occurs just after a snapshot and retention is 30 days, final physical reclamation completes in ~32–35 days (snapshot expiration + GC + block reclamation).
   • Common case (90 day retention): ~92–95 days.
   • For accounts on Dedicated with an accelerated purge request, we can schedule a special snapshot rewrite and block reclamation; that reduces window to 7–21 days depending on data size and replication statuses.

4) Cross-region considerations
- If snapshots have been replicated to another region, we verify the replication chain before purging; the deletion cannot be considered complete until the latest replica retains no references. This adds the replication verification time (usually <24 hours) to the timeline.

5) KMS key revocation
- Revoking a KMS key makes encrypted snapshots unrecoverable cryptographically — effective immediately for future restores — but the encrypted bytes remain on storage until overwritten/deprovisioned. For compliance and audit purposes we treat key revocation as an option and provide attestations.

6) Private/on-premise customers
- For Private deployments we provide an operator playbook; physical deletion timelines vary and may require customer coordination if storage is managed on-prem.

I'll add a small appendix with estimated timelines for different retention settings and a note about accelerated purge process if you'd like the MAP updated.

-Karthik

- Legal hold overrides: if Acme has an active legal hold (litigation, subpoenas), we cannot remove the data until hold is cleared; the MAP should capture the process and contact for hold release.
- Attestation: we can provide a deletion attestation letter when the purge is complete; I've attached a standard template (deletion-attestation-template.docx).
- Audit trails: we will provide audit logs showing the delete request, snapshot expiration dates, replication verification, and KMS key events. Expect those logs to be available in the Console for 90 days by default; extended retention can be included as a contract add-on.
- Regulatory nuance: if your data residency is EU and a Local Regulation requires longer retention for certain data classes, that will supersede standard timelines.
